name: South Pole
hint: the very bottom of the world, where every direction is north
hint2: Explorers raced each other across the ice to reach this spot more than a century ago.
facts: Roald Amundsen's team were the first people to reach the South Pole, in December 1911.
The South Pole sees just one sunrise and one sunset a year. It is not the same place as the South Magnetic Pole, which is thousands of kilometers away.
asks: Which spot did Roald Amundsen's team become the first people to reach, in 1911?
Where in Antarctica do people see just one sunrise and one sunset each year?

name: Mount Vinson
hint: the highest peak on the frozen continent
hint2: This peak rises in the Sentinel Range of the Ellsworth Mountains.
facts: Mount Vinson is the highest mountain in Antarctica, at 4,892 meters (16,050 feet).
Mount Vinson is one of the Seven Summits, the highest peaks of the seven continents. It is the top of a larger mountain mass called the Vinson Massif.
asks: Which is the highest mountain in Antarctica?
Which of the Seven Summits, the highest peaks of the seven continents, stands in Antarctica?

name: Mount Erebus
hint: a snowy volcano on Ross Island
hint2: This volcano rises above McMurdo Station, the big American research base.
facts: Mount Erebus is the southernmost active volcano on Earth.
Scientists have seen a lake of lava churning at the top of Mount Erebus since at least 1972.
asks: Which is the southernmost active volcano on Earth?
Which Antarctic volcano has a long-lasting lake of lava at its top?

name: Ross Ice Shelf
hint: a floating sheet of ice roughly the size of France
hint2: This ice meets the sea in a wall more than 600 kilometers long.
facts: The Ross Ice Shelf is the largest ice shelf in Antarctica, roughly the size of France.
James Clark Ross reached the Ross Ice Shelf in 1841, and early explorers called it the Barrier.
asks: Which is the largest ice shelf in Antarctica?
Which great sheet of floating ice did early explorers call the Barrier?

name: Antarctic Peninsula
hint: the long arm of Antarctica that reaches toward South America
hint2: This strip of mountains has the mildest weather on the Antarctic mainland.
facts: The Antarctic Peninsula is the part of the mainland closest to South America, about 1,000 kilometers across the Drake Passage.
The Antarctic Peninsula has the mildest weather on the Antarctic mainland, though it is still very cold.
asks: Which part of Antarctica's mainland reaches closest to South America?
Which part of Antarctica's mainland has the mildest weather?

name: Lambert Glacier
hint: a giant river of ice in East Antarctica
hint2: This great flow of ice slides north toward the Indian Ocean.
facts: Guinness World Records counts the Lambert Glacier as the longest glacier in the world.
The Lambert Glacier and the rivers of ice that join it flow into the Amery Ice Shelf.
asks: Which glacier does Guinness World Records count as the longest in the world?
Which glacier is the main river of ice feeding the Amery Ice Shelf?

name: Deception Island
hint: a horseshoe-shaped volcano in the South Shetland Islands
hint2: Ships enter the harbor inside this island through a narrow gap called Neptunes Bellows.
facts: Deception Island is a volcano with a flooded middle, and ships can sail right inside through a narrow gap.
Volcanic heat makes the beaches of Deception Island steam. Its name fits: from outside it looks like an ordinary island.
asks: Which Antarctic island lets ships sail right inside a flooded volcano?
Which Antarctic island has beaches that steam from volcanic heat?

name: Lake Vostok
hint: a huge hidden lake buried under nearly 4 kilometers of ice
hint2: Nobody can see this water, because it lies deep under the ice of East Antarctica.
facts: Lake Vostok is the largest known lake under Antarctica's ice, lying nearly 4 kilometers (2.5 miles) below the surface.
In 2012 Russian scientists drilled down to Lake Vostok. The lake is named after Vostok Station, the Russian base on the ice above it.
asks: Which is the largest known lake under Antarctica's ice?
Which hidden lake did Russian scientists drill down to in 2012?

name: Weddell Sea
hint: the icy waters east of the Antarctic Peninsula
hint2: Ernest Shackleton's ship was trapped and crushed by the ice here.
facts: Ernest Shackleton's ship Endurance sank in the Weddell Sea in 1915. Its wreck was found in 2022, about 3 kilometers down.
Scientists measured the clearest sea water on record in the Weddell Sea, seeing a disc 80 meters (262 feet) down.
asks: In which sea did Ernest Shackleton's ship Endurance sink in 1915?
Which sea off Antarctica has the clearest water ever measured?

name: Cape Denison
hint: a rocky point on Commonwealth Bay, blasted by fierce winds
hint2: Douglas Mawson's expedition built its main base on this windy shore.
facts: Cape Denison is known as the windiest place on Earth at sea level.
Douglas Mawson's expedition built its main base at Cape Denison in 1912. This is not Australia's Mawson Station, which is far to the west.
asks: Which Antarctic cape is known as the windiest place on Earth at sea level?
Which cape was the main base of Douglas Mawson's 1911-14 expedition?
